findings.title: User-controlled sortBy reaches raw ORDER BY clause
findings.description: The new appointment filter endpoint passes the sortBy query parameter straight to buildQuery(), which concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause. Any logged-in patient can alter the query and read appointments that belong to other patients.

findings.title: Stripe live secret key hard-coded in source
findings.description: A Stripe live secret key (sk_live_…redacted) is assigned to a constant in the payments client, introduced in commit a41c9e2 "fix local checkout". Anyone with repository access can create charges and refunds on the production Stripe account.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header configured
findings.description: next.config.ts defines no headers() block, so every page is served without a Content-Security-Policy. Any script injection in the portal would run with full access to the patient session.

findings.cweName: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
findings.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials allowed
findings.description: The middleware copies the request Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. Any website can make authenticated API calls on behalf of a logged-in patient and read the responses.

findings.title: Password reset tokens generated with Math.random()
findings.description: Password reset tokens are built from Math.random(), which is not a cryptographically secure generator. Tokens issued close together in time can be predicted.

findings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
findings.title: No lockout on password login
findings.description: The password login endpoint has no attempt counter or delay, unlike the OTP endpoint. Credential-stuffing lists can be tried against patient accounts at full speed.

findings.title: Profile update accepts cross-site requests
findings.description: The profile update route relies only on the session cookie and checks neither the Origin header nor a CSRF token, and the cookie's SameSite attribute was set to None for an embedded booking widget. A malicious page can change a logged-in patient's email address.
